718.stem: The population of a certain bacteria culture grows exponentially. At 12:00 pm, the population is 1000 bacteria. After 3 hours, the population reaches 2500 bacteria.

parts.latex:
The exponential function modelling the bacteria culture growth is of the form

$$P(t)=P_0a^t$$

where $P(t)$ is the population and $t$ is the time in hours since 12:00 pm.

$P_0$ and $a$ are constants.

Find the value of $P_0$ and $a$.
Find the average rate of change of the population between $t=1$ hours and $t=4$ hours. Include units in your answer.
Find the instantaneous rate of change of the population at $t=2$ hours.
Is the average rate of change constant over time in this scenario? Explain why or why not, based on the nature of exponential growth.

solutions.latex:
At $t=0$ (12:00 pm) the population is 1000, so $P_0=1000$ and $P(t)=1000(a)^t$.

Given $P(3)=2500$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2500&=1000(a)^3\\ a^3&=2.5\\ a&\approx1.3572 \end{aligned}$$
So the function is $P(t)=1000(1.3572)^t$.
criteria: Correct substitution into the model, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} P(1)&=1000(1.3572)^1\\ &=1357.2\\ P(4)&=1000(1.3572)^4\\ &\approx 3392.93 \end{aligned}$$
The average rate of change is the gradient of the chord from $t=1$ to $t=4$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Average rate}&=\dfrac{P(4)-P(1)}{4-1}\\ &\approx\dfrac{3392.93-1357.2}{3}\\ &\approx\dfrac{2035.73}{3}\\ &\approx 678.58\text{ bacteria/hour} \end{aligned}$$

meta.corrected: Corrected from source: $P(4)=1000(1.3572)^4\approx3392.93$, not $3386$, so the average rate is $\approx678.58$ bacteria/hour, not $676.27$.

solutions.latex:
Differentiate using $\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(a^t\right)=a^t\ln a$:
$$\begin{aligned} P(t)&=1000(1.3572)^t\\ P'(t)&=1000(1.3572)^t\ln 1.3572\\ P'(2)&=1000(1.3572)^2\ln 1.3572\\ &\approx 562.6 \end{aligned}$$
At 2 hours, the population is increasing at approximately $562.6$ bacteria/hour.
criteria: Correct differentiation of the function, or equivalent merit

meta.corrected: Corrected from source: $\ln 13572$ (typo) replaced by $\ln 1.3572$, and $P'(2)=1000(1.3572)^2\ln 1.3572\approx562.6$, not $560.1$.

solutions.latex: No, the average rate of change is not constant. In exponential growth, the rate increases over time because the population grows by a constant percentage, not a constant amount.
criteria: States the rate is not constant, or equivalent merit
